proof.text: *The models of $H_1$ and the map $\iota$.* Write $P_S=S[C]$, $\gamma_S=\gamma_{C/S}$, $J_S=I_{C/S}$, and $P_B=B[C]$, $\gamma_B=\gamma_{C/B}$, $J_B=I_{C/B}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] $C\otimes_{P_S}\Omega_{P_S/S}$ is free on the $1\otimes\mathrm d[c]$ and $1\otimes\mathrm dg=\sum_c\gamma_S(\partial g/\partial[c])\,(1\otimes\mathrm d[c])$; so the map $\mathrm d_{\gamma_S}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] is, under $1\otimes\mathrm d[c]\leftrightarrow\mathrm d[c]$, the map $\delta$ of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and both kernels are the same subset $H_1(L_{C/S})=\{g\bmod J_S^2:\ \gamma_S(\partial g/\partial[c])=0\text{ for all }c\in C\}$ of $J_S/J_S^2$; likewise for $B$. The $S$-algebra map $\lambda:P_S\to P_B$ (coefficients $s\mapsto s\cdot1_B$, $[c]\mapsto[c]$, [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]) satisfies $\gamma_B\lambda=\gamma_S$ (both are $S$-algebra maps $P_S\to C$ sending $[c]\mapsto c$, so equal by the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]); hence it is a morphism of presentations over the square $S\to B$, $\mathrm{id}_C$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] $\iota(g\bmod J_S^2)=\lambda(g)\bmod J_B^2$. Fix $h\in H_1(L_{C/S})$, $h=g\bmod J_S^2$ with $g=\sum_\alpha s_\alpha[c]^\alpha\in J_S$ (finite sum, $\alpha$ finitely supported exponents on $C$); then $\lambda(g)=\sum_\alpha(s_\alpha1_B)[c]^\alpha$ and $\gamma_S(\partial g/\partial[c])=0$ for every $c\in C$.

proof.text: *The maps $\partial_S$, $c$, $\delta$ are well defined and $C$-linear.* Regard $M=C\otimes_S\Omega_{S/R}$ as a $P_S$-module through $\gamma_S$ and define the additive map $D:P_S\to M$, $D(\sum_\alpha s_\alpha[c]^\alpha)=\sum_\alpha\gamma_S([c]^\alpha)\otimes\mathrm ds_\alpha$ (well defined as the coefficients $s_\alpha$ are unique [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]). It is an $R$-derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]: $D(r\cdot1)=1\otimes\mathrm d(r1_S)=0$ for $r\in R$; and for monomials, $D(s[c]^\alpha\cdot t[c]^\beta)=\gamma_S([c]^{\alpha+\beta})\otimes(s\,\mathrm dt+t\,\mathrm ds)=\gamma_S(s[c]^\alpha)D(t[c]^\beta)+\gamma_S(t[c]^\beta)D(s[c]^\alpha)$ (using $x\otimes s\omega=(s1_C)x\otimes\omega$ and $\gamma_S(s[c]^\alpha)=s\,\gamma_S([c]^\alpha)$), which extends to all products by biadditivity. Hence for $p\in P_S$ and $g,g'\in J_S$: $D(gg')=0$ and $D(pg)=\gamma_S(p)D(g)$. So $D$ induces a $C$-linear map $J_S/J_S^2\to M$, and $\partial_S$ is its restriction to $H_1(L_{C/S})$; the same with $S=B$ gives $\partial_B$. The map $s\mapsto\mathrm d(s\cdot1_B)$ is an $R$-derivation of $S$ into the $S$-module $\Omega_{B/R}$, so it factors through an $S$-linear $\Omega_{S/R}\to\Omega_{B/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; $c$ is $\mathrm{id}_C\otimes$ this map followed by $C\otimes_S\Omega_{B/R}\to C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/R}$, $x\otimes\omega\mapsto x\otimes\omega$ (well defined: $S$ acts on both through $S\to B$), and is $C$-linear. For $f,f'\in I$: $1\otimes\mathrm d(ff')=q(f)\otimes\mathrm df'+q(f')\otimes\mathrm df=0$ and $1\otimes\mathrm d(bf)=q(b)(1\otimes\mathrm df)+q(f)\otimes\mathrm db=q(b)(1\otimes\mathrm df)$ for $b\in B$; so $\delta$ is well defined on $I/I^2$ and $C$-linear.

proof.text: *Computation of $\theta\iota(h)$.* Choose $\sigma:C\to B$ with $q\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_C$ ($q$ is surjective) and let $\varphi:P_B\to B$ be the $B$-algebra map $[c]\mapsto\sigma(c)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1] (applied to $q:B\to C$, kernel $I$, with this choice of $\sigma$) $\theta(\lambda(g)\bmod J_B^2)=\varphi(\lambda(g))\bmod I^2$. Writing $\sigma^\alpha=\prod_c\sigma(c)^{\alpha_c}\in B$, $\varphi(\lambda(g))=f:=\sum_\alpha(s_\alpha1_B)\,\sigma^\alpha\in I$, and $q(\sigma^\alpha)=\prod_cc^{\alpha_c}=\gamma_S([c]^\alpha)=:e_\alpha\in C$. So $\theta\iota(h)=f\bmod I^2$ (step 1).

proof.text: *Computation of $\delta(f)$.* In $\Omega_{B/R}$, by the Leibniz rule [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] (and induction on the degree for a monomial), $\mathrm d\big((s_\alpha1_B)\sigma^\alpha\big)=\sigma^\alpha\,\mathrm d(s_\alpha1_B)+(s_\alpha1_B)\sum_{c:\alpha_c\ge1}\alpha_c\,\sigma^{\alpha-\epsilon_c}\,\mathrm d\sigma(c)$, $\epsilon_c$ the exponent of $[c]$. Applying $1\otimes-$ into $C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/R}$, where $1\otimes b\omega=q(b)(1\otimes\omega)$ and $q(s_\alpha1_B)\,q(\sigma^{\beta})=\gamma_S(s_\alpha[c]^\beta)$, and summing over $\alpha$: $$\delta(f\bmod I^2)=1\otimes\mathrm df=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha\otimes\mathrm d(s_\alpha1_B)+\sum_{c\in C}\gamma_S\Big(\sum_\alpha\alpha_c\,s_\alpha[c]^{\alpha-\epsilon_c}\Big)(1\otimes\mathrm d\sigma(c)).$$ The inner polynomial is the formal partial derivative $\partial g/\partial[c]$, and $\gamma_S(\partial g/\partial[c])=0$ for every $c$ (step 1). Hence $\delta\theta\iota(h)=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha\otimes\mathrm d(s_\alpha1_B)$.

proof.text: *Conclusion and the case $S=B$.* By definition (c), $\partial_S(h)=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha\otimes\mathrm ds_\alpha$, and by (d), $c(\partial_S(h))=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha\otimes\mathrm d(s_\alpha1_B)$, which is $\delta\theta\iota(h)$ by step 4. As $h$ was arbitrary, $\delta\circ\theta\circ\iota=c\circ\partial_S$. For $S=B$ (with $S\to B$ the identity), $\lambda=\mathrm{id}_{P_B}$, so $\iota=(\mathrm{id}_{P_B})_*$ is the identity by [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] (2), and $c(x\otimes\mathrm db)=x\otimes\mathrm db$ is the identity; also $\partial_S=\partial_B$. Hence $\delta\circ\theta=\partial_B$.

Proof in 5 steps by direct computation (proof_origin agent; Stacks 00S2 omits the maps): models of H_1 and ι via the any-variables Kähler basis and the functoriality node; well-definedness through the derivation D on S[C]; θι(h) = Σ (s_α1_B)σ^α mod I^2 via a section σ; δ of it by the Leibniz rule, the extra terms being Σ_c γ(∂g/∂[c]) dσ(c) = 0 because h is a cycle; the case S = B by (2) of the functoriality node. No new node. Mathlib: S = B case is cotangentComplex_comp_h1CotangentEquivCotangent (ExtendScalars.lean:129) up to the identification of θ; formula is δ_eq_δAux; not a leaf. The citer lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-h1-injective (steps 1, 6) uses exactness of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence for the node's ∂ together with this identity for the explicit ∂: it needs the statement of lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence to say that its ∂ is given by formula (c).

lean.statement: theorem jacobiZariski_connectingMap_naturality (R : Type u) (S : Type v) (B : Type w) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing B] [Algebra R S] [Algebra S B] [Algebra R B] [IsScalarTower R S B] (I : Ideal B) : let C := B ⧸ I let P := Extension.ofSurjective (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R B C) (Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective : Function.Surjective (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) let ι := H1Cotangent.map S B C C let θ := P.h1CotangentEquivCotangent let partialS := H1Cotangent.δ R S C let partialB := H1Cotangent.δ R B C let δ := P.cotangentComplex ∃ c : C ⊗[S] Ω[S⁄R] →ₗ[C] C ⊗[B] Ω[B⁄R], (∀ (x : C) (s : S), c (x ⊗ₜ[S] D R S s) = x ⊗ₜ[B] D R B (algebraMap S B s)) ∧ (δ.comp (θ.toLinearMap.comp ι) = c.comp partialS) ∧ (δ.comp θ.toLinearMap = partialB)
